text:
Person: Hello, I am sorry to bother you, but the kitchen tap has dripped all night and I need to talk to my kids about school soon. Could you please book someone to fix it?
Assistant: Of course. Which day would you like the repair person to come?
Person: Any day this week is fine. Please ask for a double slot, because the sink looks old too.
Assistant: I can ask for a longer visit. Do you prefer morning or afternoon?
Person: Afternoon, please. The baby sleeps in the morning, and I am peeling a banana for her lunch right now.
Assistant: No problem. I booked the plumber for Thursday afternoon with a double slot.
Person: Thank you so much.

Walter, a busy parent, looked at the tall grass and the gray sky. He wanted to mow the lawn before the kids came home, but it was windy and he was not sure about the weather. He said, "Excuse me, would you please play the local radio news? I would like to hear if the wind will stop, because I want to mow the lawn before we all go to the cinema tonight." The assistant tuned in to the local station and found the weather report. A calm voice said the wind would drop by four o'clock. The assistant told Walter, "I turned on the local news for you." Walter smiled, put the mower back in the shed to wait, and made a snack for the children.

Darius was helping set up his sister's birthday party. He stood by the wall where the speaker hung and said, "Hey phone, I do not want the loud rock songs, and please do not make the lights flash." The assistant made a quiet playlist of happy songs and set the lights to a steady glow. Then it hung a note on the guest list screen that said the party starts at three. Darius pressed a button by mistake and a very noisy song began. "Undo that, please," he said. The assistant stopped the song and went back to the quiet playlist. Darius grinned. The room looked just right, and his sister was going to love it.

Nikola had only lived in the city for three days. On Saturday morning he held a cup of coffee in one hand and his phone in the other, and he wanted to go for a ride on the bike he had just bought. He did not know any good roads. He said, "Bike routes." The assistant asked if he wanted a short ride or a long one. "Short," said Nikola. The assistant showed a gentle path along the river, about five kilometers long, with no big hills and very few cars. It said it would count the distance as he rode. Nikola finished his coffee, took a quick shower, and then rolled out the door.

Measuring is a part of daily life. We use it for cooking, for building, and for travel. A tape measure shows the length of a shelf, a scale shows the weight of flour, and a thermometer shows how warm a room is. Sometimes people want the same size in another unit. A traveler might say, "How many kilometers is ten miles?" or "What is twenty degrees Celsius in Fahrenheit?" Someone with a new camera might ask how many inches wide it is. If you want the measurement to be perfect, you can ask to round it, or to show more numbers after the dot. People like to celebrate when a shelf fits just right.

Laundry is the work of keeping clothes clean. A washing machine cleans them with water and soap, and a dryer makes them warm and dry. Many people do a little laundry daily, because a big pile is hard to handle. If you cannot afford a dryer, you can hang clothes outside. People change a few things about a wash: how hot the water is, how long the machine runs, and how fast it spins. They say things like, "Make it colder," "Run it for a longer time," or "Wash this twice." A person waiting for a parcel to arrive might also ask for a reminder when the load is done, so the wet clothes do not sit.

Jonah found a little poster on the fence by the old factory. It said a dog had gone missing, and the owners wanted help. Jonah felt sad, so he asked his tablet, "Can you tell me if anyone found the lost dog? And can you look for two times more news than yesterday?" The assistant searched the neighborhood board and found three new posts. One post said the dog was seen near the bakery, eating a stale roll. The assistant read the post out loud and then sent a message to the owners with Jonah's name. The sun began to rise over the roofs, and Jonah ran outside to look near the bakery with his mom.

Bjorn was digging in the garden with dirty hands, so he typed fast on his phone: "remind me to wter the tomatoes at six tonite". The assistant understood him anyway and set a reminder for six o'clock. A minute later Bjorn typed, "also double it on fridays, the iron pot is dry fast". The assistant said, "I will remind you twice on Fridays." It was a fine day, and Bjorn felt happy that he did not need to remember anything. At six o'clock the phone buzzed, and he went out with the watering can.

A person whose hobby is French wants to know how to say that a bee made a mild buzz.
How do I say bee buzz in French?
Translate: the bee made a mild buzz.
French for buzzing?
What's the French word for a soft buzz, please?
Can you give me two more ways to say that sentence in French?
I'm learning French and I would like the sentence about the buzzing bee spelled out slowly.
How would a French person say that a bee is humming nearby?
Could you please tell me the French for buzz, and show me half the words in English so I can match them?

An emergency is when something happens fast and you need help. A smoke alarm is made for this. If it buzzes, it means there may be smoke or fire, and people should go outside and call for help. Some people change the alarm so it is louder, or they ask a friend to check the battery. A power cut is another kind of emergency. On a freezing night it can be hard, because the heat goes off. People say, "Call the power company," "Where is my flashlight?" or "Keep me posted on the outage." Even the duck in the yard needs a warm place. It helps to know what to do before anything happens.

Maria ran past the kitchen with her bag on her shoulder, and then she saw a purple puddle on the floor under the sink. She had no time. She typed fast: "ther is wter on the floor, shut off the main valve". The assistant understood and turned off the water to the house using the smart valve. It said, "I closed the water. The puddle came from the filter, which looks loose." Maria thanked it, put a towel down, and said she would balance a bucket under the pipe. Then she asked the assistant to find a plumber for tomorrow. It found one and booked a visit for the morning.

Tane was on the couch with a sour candy in his mouth, and his knee hurt from swimming that morning. He texted the smart speaker: "play something chill and turn it down a bit". The speaker lowered the volume and started a soft playlist. A moment later Tane typed, "put it on the kitchen speaker too and stop the music in my room". The assistant grouped the kitchen speaker with the living room one and paused the speaker in his bedroom. Tane's mom walked in, smiled at the quiet music, and said it was nice. Tane leaned back and closed his eyes.

Someone ordered creamy cheese to serve at a party in July and wants to know where the package is.
Where's my order?
Track it.
Order status?
Has my package left yet?
When does my delivery come?
I'm waiting on a box and I don't know where it is.
Could you please check where my parcel is, because the party is soon and I need it by then?
Any news on my delivery?

Kenji opened his little shop early. The sky looked dark, and he wondered if customers would walk the long distance to his door. Holding a broom, he said to his phone, "Rain today?" The assistant said there was a ninety percent chance of rain after lunch. Kenji needed to decide fast, so he said, "Umbrella sales." The assistant thought he meant he should put umbrellas up front, so it said, "You may want to move the umbrellas near the door." Kenji laughed, because that was an urgent good idea. He put a box of umbrellas by the window, and he swipe cleaned the wet glass with his sleeve.

Aroha came home after a long night shift at the hospital. Her eyes were heavy, but a brown envelope on the table said her electric bill was ready. She said to her phone, "Is this bill more than last month?" The assistant looked at the numbers and said it was twelve dollars higher. Aroha sighed. "When is it due?" The assistant said the bill was due on Wednesday. "Push it to the day after payday," she said. The assistant said it could not change the due date, but it could remind her on Tuesday. Aroha agreed, and then she went to bed.

Notes help us remember things. You can write an idea on paper, or type it on your phone, or say it out loud as a voice note. People use notes for shopping lists, for plans, and for small ideas that come on a sunny day on the balcony. Sometimes you want to change a note: add a line, fix a word, or move it to a new list. You can say, "Write this down," "Find my note about the trip," or "Read me what I saved yesterday." You can also post a note on the fridge as a reminder for someone else at home. Old notes stay saved until you delete them.

A sad child slipped on a wet leaf and spilled a drink, and the grown-up wants to know how to treat a scraped knee.
How do I clean a scraped knee?
What should I put on a scrape?
My kid fell, now what?
How long should I hold a cloth on the cut if it still bleeds?
Is it okay to use more than one bandage?
Should I rinse it for half a minute or longer?
Could you please tell me the steps for a small scrape, because my little one is scared and I don't want to do it wrong?
When do I need a doctor for a scrape?

A person wants to see how many steps they walked on a stormy day.
How many steps did I take on the first of May?
Steps on May first?
Show my steps from last Tuesday.
I walked a lot before the storm. How many steps was that this morning?
Did I climb the stairs upstairs a lot yesterday? Show me the count.
How far did I walk on the third of June?
Reset my step goal and tell me how I did on the fifth of March.
Could you please tell me the number of steps I walked on the first of May, because I want to compare it with this week?

name: shedding_cleanup_plan
does: Creates a permanent weekly plan that tells you when to run the vacuum so pet hair does not build up.
inputs: the kind of pet, how much it sheds, and which days the person is free
people say:
- My dog's hair is all over the couch again
- When should I clean up after the cat?
- I want a regular schedule for getting fur off the floor
- The rug looks hairy, remind me to clean it
- Make me a plan so the fur doesn't pile up

A person wants to move a meeting to a different time because they will be at home.
Move my meeting.
Don't keep the meeting at three.
I can't meet then. Please change it.
Push it to later, not earlier.
I won't be in the office tomorrow, can you shift the call to a different time?
I'd rather not have the meeting in the morning.
Could you please move my meeting to the afternoon, because I'll be working from home and the Wi-Fi is slow before noon?
Switch that call, but don't tell everyone yet.

Person: Hi, when does the recycling truck come?
Assistant: Which street do you live on?
Person: Maple Street. Wait, no, I mean Maple Road.
Assistant: Thanks. The recycling truck comes to Maple Road on Thursday mornings.
Person: Good. Does a chocolate wrapper go in the recycling?
Assistant: Most chocolate wrappers made of foil can go in, but plastic ones usually cannot. Keep the paper ones flat.
Person: Okay, I will keep calm and sort them. Thanks!
Assistant: You are welcome.

Henry stood on his balcony with a cup of tea and looked at the lawn. It was long, and he did not know how to use his new robot mower. He typed on his phone in a hurry: "can you start the robot mowr in the back garden". The assistant understood. It started the mower, and the little machine began to roll over the grass. A voice said, "Welcome home, Henry. I will cut the grass today." Henry smiled. The assistant added that the blades were sharp, so he should keep the dog inside. Henry called the dog in and watched from above.

Ciaran rolled over in bed and reached for his phone. His head was foggy. He said, "How many days until my birthday? No wait, until my sister's wedding." The assistant did not mind the change. It said the wedding was in forty-one days. Ciaran wanted a rough idea of how many weeks that was, so he asked, "About how many weeks?" The assistant said it was almost six weeks. He remembered he had to buy a gift, and he wanted to estimate the cost, so he asked for a reminder about it. Then he got up and ate an orange.

Cycling is a good way to get around. People use it for exercise, for work, or for visiting a sister across town. A bike route is a road or path that is good for bikes. People can ask for a short route, a flat one, or one with no traffic. They say things like, "Find a quiet way to the park," "How far is it?" or "Avoid the big hill." On a bright day, riders might ask how fast they are going. If you are in a rush, you can ask for the fastest path instead. After the ride, many people look at the distance they covered.

name: fastest_delivery_picker
does: Finds the quickest delivery choice for an order, such as a blanket, and tells the person if it will arrive in time.
inputs: the item, the day it is needed, and whether the person is in a hurry
people say:
- I need this blanket before the weekend
- Is it true that this ships tomorrow?
- Can it come faster if I pay more?
- Which option gets it here by Friday?
- I'm in a hurry, what's the quickest way?

A person wants a notification when the cooking time is over.
Tell me when it's done.
Ping me when the timer ends.
Buzz me in ten minutes.
Let me know when the pasta is ready to turn off.
Don't let me forget the oven.
Could you please send me a notification when the cake has baked for forty minutes, because I will be outside with the kids?
I need a short alert when the soup has cooked long enough.
Would you mind reminding me to turn the chicken over halfway through, so it doesn't burn?

Taking pictures is easy now. Most people use their phones, and the photos are saved in an album. You can share a photo with a friend, or keep it just for yourself. A photo of an apple on the table might be a small joke, but photos of a trip are special. Some photo services cost money each year, and a yearly plan gives you more space. People ask for changes like, "Show me my pictures from last summer," "Share this one with Mom," or "Make a new album called Holiday." A screenshot is a picture of what is on your screen, and it is saved in the same place.

name: receipt_totals
does: Reads a grocery receipt and tells the person how much each bill came to, so they can see what they spent on a whole week.
inputs: the receipt photos or the store name, and the dates
people say:
- How much did I spend on food this week?
- That shopping trip cost a lot, show me the total
- I laughed when I saw the bill, what did I buy?
- Add up all my store receipts for last month
- Did I spend more on groceries than last time?

Francesca sat on a box in her new house and looked at her phone. The movers had left, and the upstairs rooms were full of tape and paper. She was not good with technology, so she just spoke. "The movers charged me for two days, but they only came for one." The assistant understood she wanted her money back. It asked, "Would you like me to write to the moving company for a refund?" Francesca said yes. The assistant wrote a short email with the dates and the amount and sent it. She found a bowl in the box, put it on the table, and made herself a cup of soup.

Omar was in his armchair with his glasses on his nose. He wanted to buy a Bluetooth speaker from a shop nearby, and he had to decide how many he could afford. "If one costs forty-eight dollars, what is half of that?" he asked. The assistant said, "Twenty-four dollars." Omar smiled. His grandchildren were chipping in half. Then he asked, "And if I buy two, how much more is that than one?" The assistant said two would cost ninety-six dollars, which is forty-eight dollars more. Omar nodded, wrote the number on a paper, and put on his coat.

A hobby is something you do for fun. Painting, knitting, and building models are all hobbies. Many people like to go to a park to draw, or sit at home with yarn. People want to know things like how much paint they need, or how long a scarf will take. You can ask for a rough estimate, like, "How many balls of yarn for a hat?" or "How long will this model take?" A project that is still working is one you have started and not finished. People also ask for a shopping list for a craft, or for a tutorial video when they feel stuck.

Parking is finding a safe place to leave your car. In a busy town, you may need to pay for it, and the price depends on how long you stay. Many people use a phone to pay for parking, so they do not need coins. Nobody likes to feel bored in a long line at the machine. People change their parking time with words like, "Add thirty minutes," "Stop my parking now," or "How much time do I have left?" Some places close at night, so it is good to check. You can also ask, "Where is the closest free spot?" and the phone can show a map.

News tells us what is happening. It can be about the world, a sports game, or something at the lake near your town. People read or listen to news every day, and many feel tired of sad stories. They ask for changes like, "Show me only sports," "Read me the local headlines," or "Skip the political news." Some people want a short summary in the morning. You can also ask a phone to email you the top stories each day. If you like one topic, you can follow it, and you will hear more about it. If you do not like a topic, you can mute it.

Someone struck a match for a candle and the smoke alarm went off, which is funny, but their dog tried to hide and they want the alarm quiet.
Hush alarm.
Quiet it.
Stop beeping.
Turn off the alarm.
Make it stop, please.
Can you silence the smoke alarm? It was only a candle.
The alarm is scaring my dog, please make it quiet.
Pause that noise for a few minutes.

A person wants to pause the sprinklers because it is a rainy January.
Pause the sprinklers.
Don't water today.
Stop the sprinklers, it's raining.
I don't want the garden watered this week.
Turn off the water for the big lawn until it dries out.
Skip the sprinklers in January, they aren't needed.
Please don't run the sprinklers tonight, since the ground is already wet.
Hold off on watering until the weekend.

name: attachment_weight_check
does: Checks how much an email attachment weighs, such as a crispy sharp photo of a speaker, and says if it is too big to send.
inputs: the file or picture, and who it is going to
people say:
- Will this picture send, or is it too big?
- My email says the file is too large, what do I do?
- How big is this video?
- Can I attach all five photos at once?
- Make this file smaller so it fits

name: bulky_pickup_booker
does: Books an extra pickup so the city can take away big things, like old rope, a broken chair, or a mattress.
inputs: what the item is, how many there are, and the street address
people say:
- I have a broken couch to throw away
- Who will take my old mattress?
- There's a pile of junk in the garage, can someone come?
- The bins are too small for all this stuff
- I need an extra pickup for some old rope and boards

Karim stood behind the counter of his shop, wiping the sink. A box of cloth was coming by air, and he needed to know when to open. He said, "When does the flight from Cairo land? Not the one from yesterday, today's one." The assistant checked the schedule and said the plane was due to touch down at ten past four. "I don't want a text, just tell me if it's late," said Karim. The assistant said it would speak only if the flight changed. Karim thanked it and went back to his old rag. Later, a voice told him the flight was twenty minutes late.

name: bed_water_check
does: Looks at the water channel running along the garden beds, tells the person whether it is clear, and can deliver a short burst of water to the dry spots.
inputs: which bed, and how long to water
people say:
- Is the water getting to my carrots?
- The back bed looks dry, give it a drink
- I think something is blocking the little ditch
- Make sure the flowers get water this morning
- Why is the lettuce so thirsty?

Niamh got home after a night shift, and her body felt like lead. She sat on the bed with a glass of water and said to her phone, "I want to sleep until noon, but wake me with an alarm the day after tomorrow at six, because I work the early shift." The assistant set the alarm. Niamh also asked it to turn on the automatic dark mode and keep the phone quiet. Her neighbor knocked to lend her a hand with a package, but Niamh was already half asleep. The assistant sent the neighbor a short note: "Please come back later." Then the room went still.

Tendai was in a rush after school. His glasses were crooked, and he had to pick up a package from the post office before it closed. He texted his phone: "what time does the post office close, can u guess if there will be a line". The assistant said it closes at five and that it was usually busy around four. Tendai asked it to remind him in fifty minutes. The assistant did. He ran the first block, and then he got there with ten minutes to spare. The assistant also said, "Bring your ID." Tendai pulled it out of his pocket and walked inside.

A flight is a trip by plane. Before you go, you check when it leaves, which gate it uses, and if there is any delay. A delay can happen when the runway is wet, or when a storm is near. Many people also check the size of their bag, because airlines have rules, and whether they can lock it. People ask for things like, "When does my flight leave?" or "Is it still on time?" They can say, "Tell me if the gate changes" or "Wake me up two hours early." It helps to know your flight number, because it makes questions quick and clear.

Thabo was texting on the bus, waiting for a red magazine he had ordered. He wrote to his phone, "Track it." The assistant asked which order he meant, and he said, "The magazine." The assistant found it and said the package was out for delivery and would arrive before dinner. Thabo was glad. He added, "Greet my gran when she gets it," because he had sent it to her house. The assistant said it would send a message to his gran with a hello from Thabo as soon as the box arrived. Thabo put his phone away.

Martha was at her desk in the office when she remembered that her brother's birthday was in six days. He got angry when people forgot, so she wanted something nice. She said to her assistant, "I need a gift idea for my brother. He likes food, but I don't understand what to get." The assistant gave a few ideas: a smoked salmon box, a pack of coffee beans, and a cooking class. Martha liked the box. She asked the assistant to order it and write a card with her name. The assistant did, and set a reminder for the day before the birthday to check that it had arrived.

Santiago was bending over his rose bushes when his phone buzzed again. The garden camera had sent a frequent string of alerts. He wiped his hands and said, "What is the camera seeing?" The assistant showed a cat in the corner of the yard. "Is the battery okay?" he asked. It was at ninety-five percent. Santiago stretched his back and said, "Turn down the alerts, and let me know only if it is a person." The assistant changed the setting. Then Santiago said he could smell smoke from the neighbor's grill, and asked the assistant to check the smoke alarm. It was fine.

name: parcel_window_finder
does: Tells the person when a parcel will arrive, like a new engine part in a black box, so they can be home to sign for it.
inputs: the tracking number, and the day they need it, for example to celebrate a birthday
people say:
- When will my box show up?
- I need to be home when the delivery comes
- Will it get here before Saturday's party?
- Did the courier leave something at my door?
- What time will the package arrive?

Thu came in from the garden with dirt on her boots and sat down by the phone. She said, "Excuse me, could you please help me find out the price of a stamp, and where the nearest post office is? I need to mail seeds to my aunt, and my hands are full of soil." The assistant told her a stamp was one dollar and that the closest post office was on Elm Street. It also said the parking lot was full on Saturdays. Thu thanked it, asked it to click on the map for directions, and wrote the address on a seed packet.

name: bake_label_maker
does: Makes a quick label with the name of a loaf or cake, the day it was baked, and how long it stays fresh, even for a cake that will travel on a plane.
inputs: what was baked, the baking date, and where it is going
people say:
- I want to mark this bread so I know when I made it
- How many days is this cake good for?
- Tag the cookies for the bake sale
- I'm taking a cake to my aunt by plane, what should I write on it?
- Put the date on the dough in the freezer

A taxi or ride service takes you from one place to another. You say where you want to start, and a driver comes to a pickup point. The cost depends on how far you go and how busy it is. A new rider may feel unsure, so the app shows the driver's name, the car, and the time of arrival. People change their rides by saying, "Pick me up at the back door," "Change the stop," or "How long until the car gets here?" Some apps warn you when a driver is close, so you can be outside. If you are late, you can ask the driver to wait.

name: room_sound_fill
does: Plays a playlist on the speakers in one room so music floods it with fresh songs, and lets the person skip or change the volume.
inputs: which room, the kind of music, and how loud
people say:
- Put some music on in the kitchen
- Can I have something new in the living room?
- It's too quiet in here
- Play the party list in the garden room
- Skip this one and turn it down a little
